text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National Development Minister Lim Hng Kiang says tightening of HDB mortgage financing rules is unlikely to hit private housing market.

- Geneva-based World Trade Organisation study places Malaysia as fastest-growing Asian country in international trade in 1990s with an average annual growth rate of 18 percent in both exports and imports.
- Businessman Neo Hong Huat says Malayan Railway (KTM) gave him authorisation to rent out KTM land to other parties.
- Singapore top insurance agent Great Eastern Life sets up subsidiary to handle billion-dollar equity investments, hoping to get better returns.
- Property stocks, sold down last Friday, likely to recover following announcement on Saturday of tighter public housing mortgage financing rules, as measures milder than expected.
- More signs of a robust US economy expected this week, which will push Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again.
- Government has spelt out details of tax concession for life insurance surplus attributable to policyholders, a proposal first made in the 1992 Budget.
- Property markets unsure of impact of measures to curb mortgage financial rules.
- Earnings of First Capital Corp and a dozen other listed companies are sensitive to measures that affect the buying power of public housing upgraders.
